status_summary: No order, statute or published ODNI policy expressly prohibiting the intelligence community from monitoring domestic disinformation was found. Executive Order 14149 (signed 2025-01-20) sets a policy against federal restrictions on protected speech, bars federal personnel from acting contrary to it, and directs the Attorney General to review federal activity of the prior four years; it does not mention the intelligence community. On 2025-08-20 the Director of National Intelligence announced ODNI 2.0, which is to reduce the office by more than 40 percent and cut spending by over $700 million a year. ODNI's accompanying fact sheet (undated; matched to the announcement) names the Foreign Malign Influence Center, calls it redundant of other intelligence community elements, says ODNI found a multi-year relationship between the center and social media companies that may have been used against Americans, and says its functions are being folded into ODNI's Mission Integration office and the National Intelligence Council. The Center is created by statute (50 U.S.C. 3059), and subsection (e) lets the Director terminate it only after 2028-12-31 and after a determination to the congressional intelligence and appropriations committees. The Center deals with foreign influence, so this is a related step rather than a domestic-disinformation prohibition. The Senate Intelligence Committee's report on the FY2027 Intelligence Authorization Act (S. 4615, S. Rept. 119-133, ordered printed 2026-08-05) describes provisions that would limit DHS Intelligence and Analysis to foreign threats and bar it from collecting on US persons (Sec. 506) and narrow the statutory definition of intelligence to foreign intelligence and counterintelligence (Sec. 609). The committee's legislation page (read 2026-10-08) lists S. 4615 as reported and placed on the Senate calendar on 2026-05-20 (Calendar No. 420) with no floor action recorded.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14149 (published 2025-01-28) declares a policy of protecting constitutionally protected speech, bars federal departments, officers and employees from acting contrary to it, and directs the Attorney General to investigate federal activities of the prior four years and recommend remedies; it does not address the intelligence community.

ODNI announces ODNI 2.0: it will reduce ODNI by more than 40 percent by the end of fiscal year 2025 and save more than $700 million a year, and its stated goals include exposing the politicization and weaponization of intelligence. The release itself does not name the Foreign Malign Influence Center or mention domestic disinformation.

ODNI's ODNI 2.0 fact sheet (undated; placed on the announcement date as an inference) describes the Foreign Malign Influence Center as redundant of the National Intelligence Council and the National Counterintelligence and Security Center, characterizes it as having been used to justify suppressing speech, and says its functions are being folded into ODNI's Mission Integration office and the National Intelligence Council. It does not use the term domestic disinformation.

Arab News publishes a report that the Foreign Malign Influence Center will be dismantled and its core functions merged elsewhere; Gabbard says it focused too heavily on elections and was used by the previous administration to justify limiting speech, while an analyst disputes that it was redundant and notes it was set to sunset at the end of 2028.

S. 4615, the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, is reported by the Senate Intelligence Committee and placed on the Senate calendar (Calendar No. 420); the committee's legislation page records no later floor action.

The Senate Intelligence Committee's report on the Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2027 (S. 4615, Senate Report 119-133) is ordered printed. It describes Sec. 506 (limits DHS Intelligence and Analysis to foreign threats and bars collection on US persons), Sec. 609 (limits the statutory definition of intelligence to foreign intelligence and counterintelligence) and Sec. 305 (limits the National Counterterrorism Center to international terrorism); additional views by Sen. Cotton and others call the defunct DHS Disinformation Governance Board an example of mission creep.
